close_reason: Closed per workspace policy. The Sloppy-Value pattern (workspace AGENTS.md) explicitly endorses the serde_json::from_value boilerplate as the consumer-side cost of round-trip fidelity and decoupling. Adding typed accessor methods on the type crate would (a) double the API surface, (b) force the type crate to depend on every typed sub-type concretely (breaking the decoupling rationale), (c) diverge from the workspace pattern on jmap-calendars-types::CalendarEvent / jmap-tasks-types::Task which have identical shape. The README already documents the per-field typed-access pattern in the 'JSContact sub-objects' section. No code change needed.
description:
ContactCard exposes 22 fields typed as `Option<serde_json::Value>` for
the RFC 9553 JSContact sub-objects (name, nicknames, organizations,
speak_to_as, titles, emails, online_services, phones, preferred_languages,
calendars, scheduling_addresses, addresses, crypto_keys, directories,
links, media, anniversaries, keywords, notes, personal_info, related_to —
22 total).

The "sloppy Value" pattern is workspace policy (AGENTS.md §Sloppy-Value)
and is justified for round-trip preservation when the schema is still
evolving. But every downstream caller wanting typed access writes the
same conversion:

```rust
let name: Name = serde_json::from_value(card.name.clone().ok_or(...)?)?;
let emails: HashMap<String, EmailAddress> =
    serde_json::from_value(card.emails.clone().ok_or(...)?)?;
let phones: HashMap<String, Phone> =
    serde_json::from_value(card.phones.clone().ok_or(...)?)?;
// ... 19 more
```

…22 times. The crate's own test suite already writes 21 of these
conversions (see lib.rs lines 686–1099). Every server crate, every client
crate, every third-party consumer pays the same boilerplate tax.

Missing safeguards:
1. No typed accessor methods (`fn name(&self) -> Option<Result<Name, _>>`)
2. No batched typed-view conversion (`fn try_typed_view(&self) -> Result<TypedView, _>`)
3. No helper module with `from_value_clone(field) -> Result<T, _>` sugar
4. No documented commitment to add accessors when the schema stabilizes

The hybrid pattern documented in crate-jmap-calendars-types/PLAN.md
(sloppy Value + opt-in typed sub-types) is in place via the jscontact
re-exports, but the ergonomic gap remains.

Two acceptable resolutions:
1. Add typed accessor methods on ContactCard (sugar; doesn't change the
   wire model). Each accessor does
   `self.field.as_ref().map(|v| serde_json::from_value(v.clone()))`.
2. Document the conversion pattern as a top-level lib.rs example
   (already partially done; expand it) AND file a follow-up to add a
   `to_typed()` accessor once the schema stabilizes.

Either way, the contract decision should be explicit in PLAN.md or a
rustdoc clause on ContactCard.

Cross-reference: workspace AGENTS.md §"Sloppy-Value pattern for
IETF-defined nested objects" — does not currently mandate accessors but
does not forbid them either.
title: ContactCard's 22 Option<serde_json::Value> fields force serde_json::from_value boilerplate in every caller
